fixed.what: The photo now fits into the space the version chip and the zoom bar leave. One ResizeObserver measures the stage, the chip's bottom and the bar's top. The top reserve is the chip's bottom + 12 (8 on a phone) and the bottom reserve is the bar's reach + 12, each at least 32 (16 on a phone). Both go on .area as inline padding, so flex centring works inside the free box. fw = min(w − 2·padX, (h − top − bottom)·aspect).

Same fit as F001, and the bar's reserve is measured, so it follows the tray hiding the bar and any change in the bar's contents. .toolbar is never wider than the stage: max-width calc(100% − 16px), scrolls sideways with its scrollbar hidden, children don't shrink, and at ≤767 the gap is 0 with a 4px pad. The −/%/+ trio stays.
The chip's height is reserved in the fit (F001's top padding), so the photo never sits under the chip, with the tray open or closed. The chip itself is unchanged.

A stable ref callback (readNatural) is used as both ref and onLoad on the motion.img. It picks up a picture that already loaded before hydration, and an equality guard avoids extra renders. The frame no longer resets to 3:2 on every version switch: the img state and setNatural(null) are removed.

The viewport carries --z. .dot, .pin and the new pin's dot get scale: calc(1/var(--z,1)), so markers, pins and their hit rings keep their size at any zoom. Pan is bounded to ±fw(z−1)/2, ±fh(z−1)/2 in every write, and in render as well (so a resize or zoom-out re-bounds it). zoomTo re-clamps at every step, not only at 100%.

A `live` state (not a ref read in render) sets data-live on .viewport while a mouse or finger pans or pinches. `.viewport[data-live] { transition: none }`, so the photo follows the hand; the cursor shows grabbing. The 150ms ease stays for the buttons, the wheel and fit.

The frame now has touch-action: none, so the editor handles its own gestures. Active pointers are tracked in a Map. One finger (or the mouse) pans once zoomed in. Two fingers pinch-zoom, 1–3×, anchored on the midpoint, and settle to the bar's 25% steps on release; a finger that stays down carries on panning. A double-tap fits (it only fits, as the verifier said). A pinch no longer zooms the whole page.

The CompareSlider gets its own .compare class (absolute, inset 0, no pointer-events rule). .fill stays only on the passive overlays. The frame's pointerdown returns straight away while comparing, so a zoomed pan can't take the slider's drag.
Same fix as F072. Mouse drag, click, and touch tap or drag now reach the slider in the editor.

CompareSlider now has touch-action: pan-y on the box, and none on the divider plus a 24px grab strip. A finger on the handle or divider grabs at once. A finger elsewhere waits: it takes the divider once it moves ≥6px more sideways than vertically, gives way to a vertical scroll, and a tap places the divider. pointercancel drops the gesture without moving anything. The mouse keeps jump-and-drag (left button only). This fixes the client link, the editor and Present together.

The progress overlay moved out of the zoomed, clipped frame and is now a direct child of .area. It dims the whole stage and is never scaled, panned or clipped. .runCard gets max-width and max-height calc(100% − 32px) with overflow-y auto, so Cancel can always be reached at 375×667.

Pin cards never render inside the photo any more. Desktop and tablet: the card is portalled to <body> (position fixed, z 95, below dialogs, sheets, snackbar and tooltips). A new useFloat hook places it: right of the pin if it fits, else left; top near the pin, clamped inside the nearest [data-pin-bounds] (the editor's stage) or the window (the client link). maxHeight comes from those bounds. It follows zoom, pan and scroll with one rect read per frame and a DOM write only when something moved. Phone (≤767, useSheetLayout): the same content goes in the house Sheet (REG-353), and the pin's dot stays on the photo. Portalled events are stopped at the card or sheet wrapper (pointerdown, click, dblclick, wheel), so a press inside a card never becomes a new pin, a fit or a zoom. The share page needs no host change.

Same as F091. The thread on a phone is a Sheet: title = author, subtitle 'Pin n · Client · 3 days ago', head actions Resolve/Remove, the note and replies in the scrolling body, the reply box and Reply in the footer. The draft is a Sheet titled with the label, the box in the body, and the hint plus Cancel / Pin it in the footer. On desktop the thread body keeps at least 72px and scrolls.

Same as F091 and F138: editor and client link both. A thread whose pin scrolls or pans out of bounds closes, per the house popover rule. A new pin's box hides until its pin is back, so a half-written note isn't lost.

The draft's hint or count now sits on its own line, with Cancel and Pin it right-aligned under it (.foot is always a column; .foot[data-row] removed). Every pin textarea gets resize: none, field-sizing: content, min 56px and max 160px.

Escape is handled inside each TextArea's own onKeyDown, through the shared NoteBox: the draft cancels and the thread closes. react-aria stops the key there, so the card never saw it. The card-root Esc stays for when focus is on the card's buttons. The sheet's Esc is also covered. This one component fixes both the editor and the client link.
Same fix as F079.

Stage side of the pin banner and quiet markers (see F018). The editor-side wiring is in crossFileRequests.

Surface squares now get a 1px overlay-40p outer ring plus elevation-2. The white border is kept, and the selected halo still wins through rule order.

Names: Marker gains optional now and pending. A surface is read as 'Label, now X, changing to Y'; a piece as 'Label, now X, Remove|Replace|Customize' (the change chips' words). Markers are wrapped in a display: contents role=group, 'Surfaces on the photo' / 'Furniture on the photo' / 'Markers on the photo'.

Stage side: the preview and the highlight each sit in an AnimatePresence motion.div wrapper using duration.toggle and ease.standard.
